2604.15279.summary: DQR (Dynamic Queue Router), a runtime that treats circuit-cutting fragments as schedulable units, so HPC centres can apply standard resource management to NISQ workloads. Evaluated on the CESGA Qmio supercomputer with its local QPU and the remote IBM Torino backend, with per-fragment failover to classical simulators.

2610.09659.summary: A communication-aware qubit-layout framework that reduces inter-node data exchange while selecting the number of computational nodes automatically. Integrated into QuCSLO, it supports dynamic node scaling, OpenQASM parsing and QuEST; evaluations on synthetic and QASMBench circuits show fewer communication cuts and runtime speedups above 2× over identity layouts, particularly for highly entangled circuits.
